method: Each claim below cites a page that was opened and read on November 1, 2026, in a browser (statute text on the Senate's Open Legislation site, court help pages, OCM pages) or, for OCM's adult-use home-cultivation FAQ PDF, through a web-fetch text conversion. A source supports only the stated claim. No service is described as available, free or guaranteed unless its own page says so. Not legal advice.

pen-222-05.limitations: Statute text, current revision from 2021-04-02. Local rules, landlord and workplace policies are not covered. Not legal advice.

pen-222-10.limitations: Statute text, current revision from 2021-04-02. Public Health Law article 13-E smoking locations are not summarized here. Not legal advice.

pen-222-15.limitations: Statute text, current revision from 2021-04-02. OCM home-cultivation regulations (9 NYCRR Part 115) add safety rules that are summarized only where OCM's own pages state them. Not legal advice.

lab-201-d.limitations: Statute text, current revision from 2023-09-08. Federal rules, safety-sensitive jobs and collective bargaining terms can change the outcome. Not legal advice.

vat-1192.limitations: Statute text, current revision from 2014-09-22. Penalties, testing and licensing consequences are in other sections and are not summarized. Not legal advice.

ocm-adult-use-info.limitations: Agency consumer summary; it cites no statute sections.

ocm-home-grow-faq.limitations: OCM adult-use home cultivation FAQ (PDF, undated; refers to rules adopted June 11, 2024 and home cultivation beginning June 26, 2024). Read through a text conversion. It does not address online, out-of-state or gifted seeds.

ocm-patients.limitations: Program instructions. Individual eligibility is decided by the certifying provider. Product availability and prices are set by registered organizations.

ocm-medical.limitations: Program overview with statistics as of October 1, 2026.

ocm-dispensing.limitations: OCM table of 30 medical dispensing facilities (6 marked temporarily closed); no page date.

ocm-verification.limitations: OCM list of licensed adult-use dispensaries; no as-of date.

ocm-licensing.limitations: Agency licensing overview. Application windows, fees and eligibility change; confirm on the linked OCM pages before applying.

ocm-symposium.limitations: Organizer event page. Agenda times are subject to change; registration terms are set by the organizer.

s3294a.limitations: Bill page shows S3294A (Sen. Cooney) as signed by the governor and lists the Cannabis Law sections it amends. Chapter number and the effective date of each provision were not confirmed.

courts-expungement.limitations: Court-system help page. Immigration consequences and non-listed offenses need individual legal advice. Not legal advice.

courts-sealing.limitations: Court-system overview of sealing. Out-of-state and federal records are not affected.

courts-160-59.limitations: Court-system instructions. The court decides each application; listed fees are as stated on the page.

courts-clean-slate.limitations: Court-system Clean Slate page. Implementation is due by November 16, 2027; no individual record should be assumed sealed yet.

lawhelpny-clean-slate.limitations: Statewide legal-information site; page last reviewed May 7, 2025. Used for the Legal Action Center referral and plain-language waiting periods only.

lac-home.limitations: Provider home page. Eligibility, capacity and case acceptance are decided by Legal Action Center.

norml-ny.limitations: NORML's national chapter listing with each chapter's website and contact. Chapter activity, meetings and membership terms were not confirmed on the chapters' own sites.

services.name: OCM list of licensed adult-use dispensaries
services.description: OCM's own list of licensed adult-use dispensaries. Licensed stores display OCM's Dispensary Verification Tool near the entrance; OCM states 757 adult-use dispensaries.
services.eligibility: Adult-use purchases are for adults 21 and older.

coverage.value: OCM lists licensed adult-use dispensaries across New York State.

evidence.value: Page states there are currently 757 adult-use cannabis dispensaries across New York State and links the Dispensary Verification Tool and the Buy Legal map.

services.name: OCM list of medical dispensing facilities
services.description: Medical dispensing facilities run by registered organizations, with county, home-delivery flag and phone. The 24 facilities not marked temporarily closed are also in this directory's location finder.
services.eligibility: For certified patients and designated caregivers. Bring the certification and a government-issued photo ID.

coverage.value: Medical dispensing facilities operated by registered organizations across New York State.

evidence.value: Table lists 30 dispensing facilities operated by 8 registered organizations, six marked temporarily closed; registered organizations handle delivery and its fees.

services.name: Get certified for the Medical Cannabis Program
services.description: A New York certifying provider (in person or telehealth) can certify a patient for any condition the provider judges suitable. The certification carries a registry ID that works immediately with a photo ID. There is no program fee, and patients may designate up to five caregivers.
services.eligibility: The certifying provider decides whether medical cannabis is appropriate.

coverage.value: New York State Medical Cannabis Program.

evidence.value: Patients are certified after consulting a NYS certifying provider in person or by telehealth for any condition the provider deems suitable; the certification's registry ID can be used immediately with a government photo ID; no fee to become a patient; up to five caregivers.
69,031 registered patients and 4,820 certifying practitioners as of October 1, 2026.

services.name: Find a certifying health care provider
services.description: OCM's open-data list of medical cannabis health care providers, which can be filtered for telemedicine.
services.eligibility: Providers decide whom they certify; appointment fees are set by the provider.

evidence.value: OCM's medical program page links this dataset as its practitioner finder.
evidence.limitations: Provider rows were not reviewed individually.

services.name: Medical home cultivation for patients and caregivers
services.description: Certified patients and designated caregivers 18 and older who are registered with the program may grow cannabis at home for a certified patient's personal use. OCM publishes a fact sheet, guide and FAQs.
services.eligibility: Registered certified patients and designated caregivers 18 and older.

evidence.value: Certified patients and designated caregivers 18+ who are registered with the Medical Cannabis Program may cultivate cannabis at home for a certified patient's personal use; plants may not be transported outside New York State.

services.name: Where New York home growers can buy seeds and immature plants
services.description: OCM says adults 21 and older can buy seeds or immature plants from an adult-use retail dispensary, microbusiness or registered organization with dispensing, and should call ahead to confirm availability. Medical home growers may buy from registered organizations.
services.eligibility: Adult-use home growers must be 21 or older; plant limits apply per person and per residence.

evidence.value: FAQ 37: adult-use consumers 21+ can purchase seeds or immature plants from an adult-use cannabis retail dispensary, microbusiness or registered organization with dispensing (ROD); contact the licensee before visiting. Certified patients and caregivers may buy from a ROD or ROND.

services.name: Marijuana expungement: automatic list and how to check
services.description: Lists the marijuana convictions expunged automatically with no motion or fee, explains how to confirm expungement with a certificate of disposition, and links the CPL 440.46-a motion form for convictions not covered.
services.eligibility: Only the listed offenses are automatic; other marijuana convictions need a motion in the court where the conviction occurred.

evidence.value: Automatic expungement without motions or fees for PL 221.05, 221.10, 221.15, 221.20, 221.35, 221.40, 222.10, 222.15, 222.25 and 222.45; the court sends no notice; a certificate of disposition shows whether a case was expunged; CPL 440.46-a motion for other marijuana convictions.

services.name: Apply to seal up to two convictions after 10 years (CPL 160.59)
services.description: Step-by-step court instructions for asking a court to seal up to two convictions (no more than one felony) after 10 crime-free years, including the certificate of disposition, notarized application, service on the District Attorney and seal verification with DCJS.
services.eligibility: Sex offenses, violent felonies and serious felonies are not eligible; the court decides each application. Expunged marijuana convictions do not count toward the limit.

evidence.value: Eligible after 10 crime-free years with no more than two misdemeanors or one felony and one misdemeanor; certificate of disposition fee $5 outside NYC and $10 in NYC; no fee to file; expunged marijuana convictions do not count.

services.name: Clean Slate Act status and review request
services.description: The court system's Clean Slate page: automatic sealing took effect November 16, 2024, with implementation due by November 16, 2027, when a form to request a manual review will be posted.
services.eligibility: Sex crimes and non-drug Class A felonies are not eligible. No individual record should be assumed sealed yet.

next_step.label: Open the court's Clean Slate page

evidence.value: Clean Slate took effect November 16, 2024; courts have until November 16, 2027 to set up automatic sealing; a manual-review request form will be available no later than that date.

rules.summary: Adults 21 and older may possess, buy and transport up to 3 ounces of cannabis and 24 grams of concentrated cannabis, and may give the same amounts to another adult 21 or older without compensation. At home, up to 5 pounds may be kept if secured from anyone under 21. 'Gifting' tied to a sale is not lawful sharing.

evidence.value: PL 222.05(1)(a)-(b): possession, purchase and transport of up to 3 oz cannabis and 24 g concentrated cannabis, and transfer without compensation of the same amounts, are lawful for persons 21+.
PL 222.15(5): up to five pounds of cannabis may be possessed in a private residence, secured from persons under 21.
Sharing without compensation is legal; any sale of a service or commodity tied to the sharing, including so-called gifting, is illegal. Effective date per the court system: March 31, 2021.

rules.summary: Adults may consume in a private home and most places where tobacco smoking is allowed, but not in a motor vehicle, where smoking or vaping is banned, on school grounds or school buses, or on federal property. Violations of the state use restrictions carry a civil penalty of up to $25 or up to 20 hours of community service.

evidence.value: PL 222.10: no smoking or vaping where prohibited under Public Health Law article 13-E, and no smoking, vaping or ingesting on school grounds or school buses; civil penalty up to $25 or up to 20 hours of community service.
Legal in a private home or most places tobacco can be consumed, except a motor vehicle; illegal where tobacco smoking is prohibited and on federal property.

rules.summary: Adults 21 and older may grow up to 3 mature and 3 immature plants, with no more than 6 mature and 6 immature plants per residence, only at their private residence and secured from anyone under 21. Selling homegrown cannabis is illegal, and flammable solvents are banned for home processing. Localities may regulate but not effectively ban home growing.

evidence.value: PL 222.15(1)-(3), (6): 3 mature and 3 immature plants per person, 6 and 6 per private residence, cultivation only at a private residence, no one under 21; localities may regulate with penalties of $200 or less but may not completely or essentially prohibit it.
Revised Personal Home Cultivation Regulations adopted June 11, 2024; adult-use home cultivation began June 26, 2024; no person may sell, barter or exchange cannabis without a license.
Flammable materials are prohibited for home processing; plants must be secured and odor controlled.

rules.summary: Employers generally may not act against workers for lawful off-duty cannabis use away from the workplace and without employer property. Employers may still act when required by state or federal law, when a worker shows specific articulable signs of impairment on the job, or when allowing it would violate federal law or risk a federal contract or funding.

evidence.value: Labor Law 201-d(2)(b)-(c) protects legal use of consumable products and recreational activities, including cannabis in accordance with state law, outside work hours and off premises; 201-d(4-a) permits action required by law, for articulable on-the-job impairment, or to avoid violating federal law or losing a federal contract or funding.

rules.summary: Driving while impaired by a drug, or by drugs combined with alcohol, is a crime and is treated like alcohol-impaired driving. Cannabis in a vehicle must be in a closed container, and smoking cannabis in a vehicle is illegal for drivers and passengers.

evidence.value: VTL 1192(4) and (4-a) prohibit operating a motor vehicle while ability is impaired by a drug or by the combined influence of drugs or alcohol and drugs. Open Legislation shows the current revision from 2014-09-22; that date is used as the rule's effective date.
Cannabis in a vehicle should be in a closed container; open containers and smoking in a vehicle, moving or parked, are illegal; driving under the influence is treated like alcohol-related DUI.

rules.summary: Convictions under the listed marijuana offenses (possession up to 16 ounces or sale up to 25 grams) are expunged automatically, with no motion or fee and no notice sent. Expunged cases do not appear on background checks and need not be disclosed. Other marijuana convictions require a CPL 440.46-a motion.

evidence.value: Effective March 31, 2021; automatic expungement of PL 221.05, 221.10, 221.15, 221.20, 221.35, 221.40, 222.10, 222.15, 222.25 and 222.45 convictions; no notice from the court; expunged charges do not show on background checks and need not be disclosed; CPL 440.46-a motion for others.

rules.summary: The Clean Slate Act provides automatic sealing of eligible convictions for certain civil background checks: misdemeanors after three years and most felonies after eight years without new convictions. Courts have until November 16, 2027 to finish setting it up. Sex crimes and non-drug Class A felonies are not eligible.

evidence.value: Took effect November 16, 2024; implementation due by November 16, 2027; sex crimes and non-drug Class A felonies are not eligible.
Misdemeanors sealed after three years and most felonies after eight years without new convictions; parole or probation must be finished.
evidence.limitations: Secondary plain-language summary; the statute is CPL 160.57.

rules.summary: A New York certifying provider may certify a patient for any condition the provider judges suitable. Patients or caregivers may buy up to a 60-day supply or 3 ounces of cannabis or 24 grams of concentrate, whichever is greater, and certifications may run up to two years. S3294A, signed in 2025, also lets registered patients and caregivers 18 and older grow at home and lets patients certified in other states buy here.

evidence.value: Certification for any condition the provider deems suitable; purchases up to a 60-day supply or 3 oz/24 g, whichever is greater; certification may be issued for less than two years; patients and caregivers 18+ may grow at home.
S3294A (2025-2026, Sen. Cooney) is shown as signed by the governor and amends Cannabis Law sections 3, 30, 31, 32, 34, 37, 41 and 42.
evidence.limitations: Out-of-state patient purchases are described in OCM's November 25, 2025 release; implementation status of each provision was not confirmed. The MRTA date is used as the rule's effective date.
